mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi replacement engine typically costs £450-£1,000 for a used unit, £950-£1,600 for a reconditioned unit, or £1,200-£2,100 for a rebuilt unit with 12-month warranty. Supply & fit labour adds approximately £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR cooler failure in a Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include frequent low coolant warnings without visible external leaks, white smoke from the exhaust, engine overheating, and a rough idle. If left unaddressed, coolant loss can lead to serious engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a 508 1.6 BlueHDi worth £4,000-£10,000, replacement is often worthwhile if the rest of the car is in good condition. If the vehicle is worth under £4,000, a used engine or scrapping may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi engines are dispatched within 24-48 hours, with supply & fit installation typically completed within 1-2 working days at approved garages.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi replacement engines?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rebuilt Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi engines include a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Used engines typically carry 3-6 months cover depending on supplier terms. Always verify warranty terms before purchase.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the 1.6 BlueHDi and the 1.5 BlueHDi in the Peugeot 508?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 1.6 BlueHDi (DV6) was fitted to the first-generation 508 (2011-2018) and produces 112-120hp. The 1.5 BlueHDi (DV5) replaced it on the second-generation 508 (2018 onwards), offering 130hp with improved emissions but introducing its own AdBlue-related failure points.

historyTimeline.intro: The 1.6 BlueHDi joined the Peugeot 508 range as the entry-level diesel option for the first-generation model, offering a balance of economy and adequate performance for UK buyers before being phased out in favour of the smaller 1.5 BlueHDi on the second-generation 508.

milestones.description: DV6 HDi (1.6L, 112-115hp) launched with the original Gen 1 508 saloon and SW estate
DV6 updated to BlueHDi specification for Euro 6 emissions compliance
Facelift styling with vertical grille; BlueHDi continues with minor calibration updates
1.6 BlueHDi discontinued on Gen 2 508, replaced by 1.5 DV5 BlueHDi

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi is a generally robust workhorse diesel, but EGR cooler cracking and DPF regeneration failures dominate replacement enquiries. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Use the problem groups below to compare repair costs versus replacement value for your specific 1.6 BlueHDi.

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Cracking - Why DV6 1.6 BlueHDi Diesel Engines Lose Coolant
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler on the DV6 family is prone to thermal stress cracking, allowing coolant to leak into the exhaust or combustion chambers, triggering low coolant warnings and potential overheating.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked EGR cooler; flush cooling system; reset ECU
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace EGR cooler; perform forced DPF regeneration; clean EGR valve
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if DPF warnings are also present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt DV6 with upgraded EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine has 110k+ miles or shows additional wear

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi of 2014-2018 vintage is worth approximately £4,000-£10,000 depending on mileage and condition [INDUSTRY ESTIMATE]. For vehicles under £5,000, a used engine or targeted EGR repair typically offers better value than a full rebuilt unit. For vehicles worth £5,000-£8,000, reconditioned or rebuilt is viable if keeping the car 2+ years.
problems.recommendation: On a Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi, an EGR cooler replacement at the first sign of coolant loss is cost-effective and prevents more serious engine damage. If the vehicle has exceeded 110,000 miles or shows additional diesel wear signs, a rebuilt DV6 with upgraded components offers better long-term reliability.

problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Failure - Why 1.6 BlueHDi Diesels Lose Power
problems.rootCause: Short-journey driving prevents active DPF regeneration, causing soot accumulation that blocks exhaust flow and triggers power-limiting fault codes.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Diagnostic-led forced DPF burn; clean EGR valve; reset adaptation
repairOptions.longevity: Works if blockage is mild and driving patterns change

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove DPF; thermal/chemical clean; pressure test; reinstall with new gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Extends DPF life 30k-50k miles if driving habits improve

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt DV6; include DPF clean or replacement; 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Best value when engine shows additional wear or DPF is beyond cleaning

problems.vehicleValueCheck: For a Peugeot 508 1.6 BlueHDi used primarily for motorway driving, a professional DPF clean often resolves the issue cost-effectively. For urban-use vehicles with recurring DPF warnings, a rebuilt diesel engine with updated EGR and DPF components provides more reliable long-term ownership.
problems.recommendation: If your 1.6 BlueHDi is used mainly for short urban trips, consider a forced regeneration and EGR clean first. If DPF warnings recur within 12 months or the vehicle is high-mileage, a rebuilt DV6 with upgraded components eliminates the repeat risk and offers better long-term value than repeated repairs.
